Amended data topics within data collections

Data collection SDL ref

Road condition data (DfT) – Local authorities will move from the SCANNER standard to the new British Standards Institute (BSI) Publicly Accepted Specification (PAS) 2161 developed by DfT, local government and the wider industry for reporting the percentage of A roads and motorways in each 5 categories of condition still in a single annual survey. 130-01

Road condition data (DfT) – Local authorities will move from the SCANNER standard to the new British Standards Institute (BSI) Publicly Accepted Specification (PAS) 2161 developed by DfT, local government and the wider industry for reporting the percentage of B and C roads in each 5 categories of condition separately but still in a single annual survey. 130-02

Revenue Outturn (MHCLG) – Introduction of new ‘recharges’ column will allow for transparent reporting of the value of overheads that have been internally recharged from other parts of the revenue account, in turn improving consistency across authorities’ returns and enabling better benchmarking. A breakdown of Adult Social Care other income will allow for transparent reporting of NHS contributions and enable the underlying figures on NHS-funded expenditure on social care to be included in figure of expenditure on adult social care. 028-00

Revenue Outturn - Debt memorandum (MHCLG) – Addition of new debt cost memorandum table to the Revenue Outturn collection. 028-00

Food Standards (LA food law enforcement monitoring return) – The LA Data project will introduce a new mechanism for monitoring and reporting on the delivery of official food and feed controls by local authorities across England, Wales, and Northern Ireland. It aims to provide more effective and timely performance and reporting data on the delivery of official controls undertaken by LAs and will replace the current LA question-based surveys. 191-00

Early Years Census – Moving the census from an annual to a termly census data collection for all the EY entitlements, beginning from summer 2026. 096-00

Animal Health & Welfare Management and Enforcement System (AMES) – Simplification of data requirement by no longer requesting data on an inspection-by-inspection basis but instead moving to a biannual aggregated return. 071-00

Data collection SDL ref

Food Hygiene and Food Standards (Local Authority food law enforcement monitoring returns for both)

The data topics pertaining to food hygiene and food standards sections of the LAEMS data collection have been amended or cancelled

The Local Authority (LA) data required is similar to that collected previously, but in many cases is simply less detailed. The use of LAEMS (Local Authority Enforcement Monitoring System) has ceased and bespoke returns / short interim ‘temperature check’ surveys have been introduced as a temporary measure, to facilitate the monitoring of the LA Covid-19 Recovery Plan and to provide year end monitoring data. New official control delivery models for food hygiene and food standards controls and a new approach for data collection on the delivery of official food and feed controls are currently in development. A new system should be in place by April 2023

The data collected in each quarterly ‘temperature check’ survey (July 2022, Oct 2022, Jan 2023) and end of year survey April 2023 are subject to change, with unchanged LA burden. These surveys will be reflective and forward looking, with the objective of evidencing performance against the previous milestone, whilst assessing preparedness to achieve the next one. 190-00 and 191-00
